items.stem: Which of the five S's does this represent? Unneeded jigs are tagged and moved to a holding area.
A project needs a $30,000 investment and saves $20,000 per year. What is the payback period in years?
Which Lean term does this describe? A light that signals the line has stopped for a problem.
items.explanation: Andon. Andon is the visual or audible alert.

items.stem: A process has three steps with first-time yields of 0.98, 0.98, and 0.97. What is the rolled throughput yield?
items.explanation: RTY = 0.98 × 0.98 × 0.97 = 0.9316, or 93.2%. It is always at or below the lowest step yield.

items.stem: An audit of 500 units, each with 3 opportunities for a defect, finds 25 defects. What is the DPMO?
Which cost-of-quality category is this? The cost of training operators on a new work standard.
items.explanation: Prevention. Stopping defects before they happen is prevention.

items.stem: Which cost-of-quality category is this? The cost of a customer return and a replacement shipment.
items.explanation: External failure. The defect reached the customer.

items.stem: A process adds 12 minutes of value inside a total lead time of 3 hours. What is the process cycle efficiency?
A project costs $20,000 and delivers $100,000 in benefits. What is the ROI?
A process produces 8,000 defects per million opportunities. Using the Z table and the 1.5σ shift convention, what is its sigma level?
items.explanation: Tail area 0.008000 gives a long-term Z of 2.41. Sigma level = 2.41 + 1.5 = 3.91σ.

items.stem: Which waste (IASSC wording) does this describe? A plant builds 1,200 units this week against an order for 800.
items.explanation: Overproduction. Making more than the customer needs is overproduction.

items.stem: Which role does this describe? Takes over the control plan after the project closes.
items.explanation: Process Owner. The process owner carries the gains forward.

items.stem: Which of the five S's does this represent? Each hand tool gets a labeled outline on the wall.
items.explanation: Straighten. A place for everything is Straighten.

items.stem: Which Lean term does this describe? Walking the floor to observe the work where it happens.
items.explanation: Gemba. Gemba is where the work happens.

items.stem: Which waste (IASSC wording) does this describe? A packer walks to the far end of the room to get tape for each carton.
items.explanation: Motion. Unnecessary movement by people is motion.

items.stem: A process has 48 orders in progress and completes 12 orders per day. What is the average lead time in days?
items.explanation: Little's Law: lead time = WIP ÷ throughput = 48 ÷ 12 = 4.00 days.

items.stem: Which cost-of-quality category is this? The cost of incoming inspection of purchased parts.
Which waste (IASSC wording) does this describe? Finished invoices wait three days in a manager's tray for a signature.
items.explanation: Waiting. Idle time between steps is waiting.

items.stem: Which waste (IASSC wording) does this describe? Pallets are moved by forklift from the receiving dock to a storage building and then to the line.
items.explanation: Conveyance. Moving material between places is conveyance.

items.stem: A 450-minute shift includes 30 minutes of breaks, and demand is 100 units per shift. What is the takt time in minutes per unit?
items.explanation: Available time = 450 − 30 = 420 minutes. Takt = 420 ÷ 100 = 4.20 minutes per unit.

items.stem: Which measurement system error does this describe? Two operators consistently get different averages on the same parts.
Which graph is best for this purpose? Compare the spread of fill weights across four machines.
items.explanation: Boxplot. Boxplots compare groups side by side.

items.stem: Which measurement system error does this describe? The same operator gets different readings measuring one part five times.
items.explanation: Repeatability. Variation with the same operator and gage is repeatability.

items.stem: On the common FMEA scale, which Detection rating means the control is least likely to catch the failure?
items.explanation: Detection is reverse-scaled, so 10 means the failure would almost certainly escape.

items.stem: What type of data is this? Seconds to close a support ticket.
items.explanation: Continuous. Time is measured and can take any value.

items.stem: What type of data is this? The number of scratches on a panel.
items.explanation: Discrete (count). A count of defects is discrete.

items.stem: A stable process has mean 103, within-subgroup standard deviation 2, USL = 115, and LSL = 85. What is Cpk?
items.explanation: Cpu = 2.00, Cpl = 3.00. Cpk is the smaller, 2.00. (Cp would be 2.50.)

items.stem: A value stream map shows three processing steps of 5, 5, and 5 minutes, with a total of 4 hours of waiting. Assuming all processing is value-added, what is the process cycle efficiency?
A stable process has Cpk = 1.5. What is its approximate short-term sigma level?
A failure mode has Severity 8, Occurrence 7, and Detection 4. What is its RPN?
Which measurement system error does this describe? A gage reads accurately on small parts but reads higher and higher on large parts.
items.explanation: Linearity. Bias that changes across the range is linearity.

items.stem: A master part is certified at 25.00. A gage's average reading on it is 24.94. What is the bias?
In an attribute agreement study the observed agreement is 0.82 and the agreement expected by chance is 0.55. What is kappa?
Failure mode A has S 10, O 1, D 1 (RPN 10). Failure mode B has S 3, O 4, D 3 (RPN 36). What is the best approach?

options.html: Give A specific attention because of its severity, in addition to ranking by RPN
Ignore A because its RPN is lower
Address only B because it has the higher RPN

items.explanation: A very high severity needs attention regardless of RPN.

items.stem: A Gage R&R study gives repeatability SD = 0.05, reproducibility SD = 0.04, and part-to-part SD = 0.8. What is %Study Variation?
In a C&E matrix the output importances are 8 and 3. An input is rated 9 against the first output and 3 against the second. What is its score?
A sample has the values 23, 26, 23, 25, 25. What is the sample standard deviation?
A process is normal with mean 50 and standard deviation 5. What percent of output exceeds 55?
A Gage R&R study has GRR SD = 0.045 and part-to-part SD = 0.2. What is the number of distinct categories (software truncates the result)?
Two independent parts are stacked. Their standard deviations are 3 and 12. What is the standard deviation of the stack?
A process has a 10% defective rate. In a sample of 6, what is the probability of exactly 2 defective?
A sample of 9 has a mean of 80 and a standard deviation of 6. What is the upper limit of the 95% confidence interval for the mean?
Two samples give defective rates of 20% (n = 200) and 10% (n = 300). Using the Reference Document's unpooled form, what is the z statistic?
Which hypothesis test fits? Mean thickness from two independent suppliers is compared (normal data).
items.explanation: 2-sample t-test. Two independent normal groups compared on the mean.

items.stem: A process has σ = 8. What is the standard error of the mean for samples of n = 16?
Which describes this situation? A real 20% speed improvement goes undetected because the sample was small.
items.explanation: Type II error. Failing to detect a real difference is Type II.

items.stem: Which hypothesis test fits? A team asks whether fill volume varies more on nozzle A than on nozzle B (normal data).
items.explanation: F test for two variances. A question about variation calls for a variance test.

items.stem: 16 operators are measured before and after training. The mean difference is 1.0 and the standard deviation of the differences is 2. What is the paired t statistic?
In an ANOVA, SS between = 60 with 2 df, and SS within = 90 with 20 df. What is F?
Which hypothesis test fits? Skewed delivery times from two carriers are compared.
Which distribution models this? The number of pinholes in a casting.
items.explanation: Poisson. Counts of defects over a unit follow the Poisson pattern.

items.stem: Which hypothesis test fits? Mean yield at five reactor temperatures is compared (normal data).
items.explanation: One-way ANOVA. Three or more normal groups compared on the mean.

items.stem: In a contingency table a cell has row total 80, column total 90, and grand total 200. What is the expected count?
A sample of 16 has mean 54 and standard deviation 5. What is the 1-sample t statistic for H0: μ = 50?
Which describes this situation? A team declares a new fixture reduces scrap, but scrap is actually unchanged.
items.explanation: Type I error. Rejecting a true null is a Type I error.

items.stem: Which hypothesis test fits? Skewed ticket resolution times are compared across four support teams.
items.explanation: Kruskal-Wallis. Three or more independent non-normal groups.

items.stem: Which distribution models this? The number of defective units in a sample of 25.
items.explanation: Binomial. Defectives in a fixed number of trials are binomial.

items.stem: Defects occur at an average of 1 per unit. What is the probability a unit has exactly 2 defects?
Which hypothesis test fits? The same 10 technicians are timed on a task before and after a new tool is introduced (differences are normal).
items.explanation: Paired t-test. The same units are measured twice.

items.stem: How many observations are needed to estimate a mean to within ±4 at 95% confidence if σ = 10?
A correlation of r = 0.9 is found between two variables. What is the coefficient of determination r²?
A simple regression with n = 15 has SST = 200 and SSE = 60. What is F?
True or False: At the same X, a prediction interval is narrower than the confidence interval.
A regression slope is 2.4 with a standard error of 0.5. What is the t statistic for H0: slope = 0?
True or False: Adding any term to a regression model can never lower R².
items.explanation: R² never decreases when a term is added.

items.stem: For a data set, Sxy = 30, Sxx = 40, and Syy = 60. What is the correlation coefficient r?
A model with n = 30 observations and k = 2 predictors has R² = 0.9. What is the adjusted R²?
An observed value is 12 and the fitted value is 10.4. What is the residual?
The 95% confidence interval for a regression slope is 0.2 to 1.4. What is the conclusion?

options.html: The slope differs significantly from zero because the interval excludes zero

items.explanation: An interval that excludes 0 corresponds to rejecting slope = 0.

items.stem: True or False: The residuals from a least-squares line sum to zero.
A fitted line is Ŷ = 5 − 2X. What is the predicted value at X = 4?
A regression has R² = 0.81. Which statement is correct?

options.html: 81% of the variation in Y is explained by the model

items.explanation: R² is the share of variation in Y explained.

items.stem: What does this residual pattern indicate? Residuals plotted in collection order drift steadily upward.
items.explanation: Dependence over time. A pattern versus order means dependence or a time effect.

items.stem: Regressing one predictor on the others gives R² = 0.8. What is its VIF?
What does this residual pattern indicate? One point lies far from the rest and the fitted line tilts toward it.
items.explanation: An influential outlier. An extreme point that pulls the line is influential.

items.stem: What does this residual pattern indicate? Residuals versus fits show a clear U shape.
items.explanation: Wrong functional form (curved). A curve means the straight-line model is wrong.

items.stem: A model fitted on X values from 10 to 40 is used to predict Y at X = 90. What is the main problem?
items.explanation: The relationship may not hold outside the data.

items.stem: True or False: A strong correlation proves that X causes Y.
What does this residual pattern indicate? Residuals versus fits show a funnel that opens to the right.
items.explanation: Non-constant variance. A funnel means the spread changes with the fitted value.

items.stem: A correlation of r = −0.7 indicates:

options.html: A moderately strong negative linear relationship

items.explanation: The sign gives direction and the size gives strength.

items.stem: An individuals chart has X̄ = 50 and an average moving range of 2. Using the n = 2 constants (d2 = 1.128), what is the UCL of the individuals chart?
How is this device classified? A beeper sounds when the wrong bin is chosen, but the line keeps running.
items.explanation: Warning (detection) type. It signals but does not stop the process.

items.stem: An Xbar-S chart uses subgroups of n = 8, with S̄ = 2. What is the UCL of the S chart?
Using the standardized CuSum Sₙ = (1 ÷ σ) × Σ(xᵢ − T), a process has T = 100, σ = 2, and four readings 99, 101, 101, 102. What is S₄?
Which control chart fits? Late orders are counted out of a daily volume that varies.
items.explanation: p chart. Defective units with varying sample size use a p chart.

items.stem: A u chart has ū = 0.8 defects per unit and an average subgroup size of 10. What is the upper control limit?
A point beyond the upper control limit has a known cause (a broken tool). What is the best next step?

options.html: Delete the point and recompute the limits immediately
Contain, investigate and correct the cause, and recompute limits only after a verified change and stable baseline

items.explanation: Do not recompute limits just because a point is out of control.

items.stem: An EWMA chart uses λ = 0.2 and a starting value (EWMA₀) of 100. The first reading is 110. What is EWMA₁?
Which control chart fits? One temperature reading per batch, one batch per day.
An np chart uses samples of n = 100, and the average defective rate is p̄ = 0.03. What is the lower control limit?
items.explanation: np̄ = 3. The computed lower limit is -2.12, which is negative, so it is set to 0.

items.stem: Nine points in a row fall above the center line, all inside the control limits. What is the best reading?

options.html: A likely shift in the mean; investigate for a special cause

items.explanation: Nine in a row on one side is a Nelson signal for a shift.

items.stem: A c chart tracks defects on identical units with an average of 25 defects per unit. What is the upper control limit?
An Xbar-S chart uses subgroups of n = 8, with X̿ = 50 and S̄ = 2. What is the UCL of the Xbar chart?
How is this device classified? A fixture only accepts a part in one orientation.
items.explanation: Prevention (control) type. The error cannot be made.

items.stem: A p chart has p̄ = 0.03 and an average subgroup size of 100. What is the upper control limit?
Demand is 90 units per hour, the replenishment lead time is 10 minutes, the safety factor is 20%, and each container holds 12 units. How many kanbans are needed?
Which control chart fits? Five parts are measured each hour.
items.explanation: Xbar-R. Continuous subgroups of 2 to 10 use Xbar-R.

items.stem: An Xbar-R chart uses subgroups of n = 3, with R̄ = 8. What is the UCL of the R chart?
Which control chart fits? Fifteen readings are taken each hour from a multi-head machine.
An Xbar-R chart uses subgroups of n = 5, with X̿ = 100 and R̄ = 4. Using the constants table, what is the UCL of the Xbar chart?
